content:
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
DevOps & Platform Engineering | QA Automation
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Infrastructure-focused QA Automation Engineer with 7 years of experience, including hands-on ownership of CI/CD pipelines and test infrastructure for three product teams. Improved pipeline speed and reliability, and built short-lived Kubernetes test environments using Helm and GitLab CI. Brings additional personal experience with k3s, GitOps, monitoring and Terraform-based VPS provisioning. Transitioning toward a full-time DevOps or platform engineering role.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
CI/CD and containers: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm
Infrastructure and platforms: Kubernetes (Helm workloads with namespace-level access; personal k3s cluster), Terraform (personal project), Argo CD, Ansible (basic), Linux
Monitoring and data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL
Programming and testing: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Cloud learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, plus artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end testing into its own stage; monthly CI runner costs fell by about 30%.
- Built merge-request ephemeral environments using Docker Compose and later Helm on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster; environments include the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, and are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Developed Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test-data seeding.
- Built a flaky-test dashboard using CI results, PostgreSQL and Grafana to help teams identify and address recurring failures.
- Wrote an internal guide to the CI system used in team onboarding.
- Mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects using manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi 5 devices, with applications deployed from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Delivered short-lived environments for merge requests, deployed through GitLab CI and Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster.
- Enabled QA and product teams to review changes before merge and run end-to-end tests against seeded environments.
- Automated environment removal after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATION AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam scheduled for January 2027; currently studying

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured and credible CV. It presents a clear QA-to-DevOps transition, uses quantified achievements, distinguishes professional Kubernetes access from personal infrastructure work, and avoids overstating the pending CKA certification. The experience bullets are specific and demonstrate ownership, automation, reliability improvements, observability and stakeholder enablement. The main content limitation is that the CV is stronger for CI/CD and test infrastructure than for cloud infrastructure architecture, networking and security. Its scope is nevertheless presented honestly and professionally.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, readable text formatting and relevant keyword groupings. It should parse well and has strong keyword coverage for GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, Linux, Python, AWS, Prometheus, Grafana and PostgreSQL. AI/ATS screening probability is high for QA automation, CI/CD and junior-to-mid DevOps/platform roles, but moderate for this specific contractor role because the CV does not contain Terragrunt, mutual TLS/mTLS, network design, systems architecture or production cloud operations. Supported technical terms such as Git, GitLab API, cert-manager, Traefik and pytest-xdist are present in the candidate material but are not fully represented in the main Technical Skills section.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document demonstrates hands-on infrastructure-related engineering through GitLab CI ownership, ephemeral Kubernetes environments, Helm, Docker Compose, test-environment lifecycle automation, observability dashboards and personal k3s/Terraform work. It also shows analytical thinking and clear communication through the pipeline optimization metrics, flaky-test reduction, onboarding guide and support for QA and product teams. AWS exposure is shown at a basic learning level, which is relevant but limited. The candidate material does not support strong Terraform and Terragrunt, mTLS, train/IoT/remote-device integration, backend or full-stack engineering, or virtual-machine experience; these are genuine role-alignment gaps rather than document defects. The CV is therefore a credible but not complete match for a cloud infrastructure contractor expected to design production connectivity architecture from the start.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Technical Skills section, expand the supported infrastructure and automation keywords without implying unsupported expertise. Add “Git” and “GitLab API” under CI/CD and automation; add “Argo CD,” “cert-manager,” “Traefik,” and “TLS certificate management” under Infrastructure and platforms; add “pytest-xdist” under Programming and testing. These terms are supported by the candidate’s portfolio and improve ATS retrieval for platform and observability work.
2. In the Professional Summary, make the candidate’s strongest job-relevant scope more explicit by changing the opening to: “Infrastructure-focused QA Automation Engineer with 7 years of experience, including hands-on ownership of CI/CD pipelines, ephemeral Kubernetes environments and test infrastructure for three product teams.” Keep the existing qualification about namespace-level Kubernetes access and personal infrastructure work so the scope remains truthful.
3. In the Odrava Health Software experience section, revise the ephemeral-environment bullet to include the stakeholder outcome already supported elsewhere in the CV: “Built merge-request ephemeral environments using Docker Compose and later Helm on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster, including the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data; enabled QA and product teams to review changes and run end-to-end tests before merge.”
4. In the Selected Infrastructure Projects section under “Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps,” change “Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS” to “Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress, and cert-manager for TLS certificate management.” This uses terminology closer to the advertisement while avoiding an unsupported claim of mutual TLS.
5. In the Technical Skills section, retain the qualification limits already shown for Terraform, AWS and Kubernetes. Do not label Terraform as “strong,” do not add Terragrunt or mTLS, and do not imply production AWS or cluster-administration experience, because the candidate information does not support those claims.
